children: stock was volatile as the company's
jumped past consensus, while long-term dividend guidance disappointed.
Shares were 1.99% higher at $40.47 during post-market trading on Thursday, after trading about 1.50% lower.
Adjusted EPS came in at $0.82 during Q3, compared to $0.80 in the same period a year ago and above the Visible Alpha consensus of $0.73.
Total revenue jumped to $114.46M from $103.06M. Interest and rental income increased to $82.59M from $68.98M a year ago.

"These factors have translated into superb financial results through the first three quarters of 2026, with our Managed Assets increasing nearly $3B to $19B, adjusted recurring net investment income growing 23%, and adjusted EPS by 15% year-to-date, and our adjusted ROE rising to 15.6%," said CEO Jeffrey Lipson.
HASI reaffirmed its adjusted EPS guidance to be in the range of $3.55 to $3.65.

The sustainable infrastructure assets investor maintained its quarterly cash dividend at $0.425 per share of common stock; payable on January 8, 2027, to stockholders of record as of December 29, 2026.
The company said it expects distributions of annual dividends per share to decline to less than 50% of the annual adjusted EPS by 2028 and to less than 40% by 2030.
Additionally, HASI expects minimal share issuances through its at-the-market program for the full year 2026.

title: HASI trades mixed amid Q3 earnings beat, disappointing long-term dividend guide
